title: The first 56 characters of a 69-character M address: checksum-valid prefix that must not decode
why: A VARCHAR(56) column truncates a 69-character M address to this string (wallet-backend#716). Its CRC is not checked against the full address, so a decoder that skips the per-type length check reads it as a valid M address with a 32-byte payload, dropping the muxed id.

known_divergences.detail: Executed: v0.7.1 strkey.Decode returns a 32-byte payload under the M version byte instead of an error; v0.7.2 rejects it. Earlier versions were not run.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9S6 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on go v0.7.1; xcc conform run --columns 'go@v0.7.1' --entries 'strkey/truncated-muxed-address-56-chars'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: the v16 StrKey decoder (unchanged since 16.0.0) checks the checksum but not the per-type payload rules and returns a payload. The strict decoder exists only on the v17 line, where 17.2.0 and later reject this vector.
